_comment: Benchmark registry — a CLOSED vocabulary, exactly like the topics list in taxonomy.json, and read by both the Astro site (src/benchmarks.ts) and the Python pipeline (scripts/core/registry.py) so the two can never drift. A benchmark slug that is not in this file is DROPPED, never invented: an adapter that meets an unknown benchmark logs it and moves on. Scope is text/reasoning benchmarks only — no multimodal, no agentic-specific suites, no cost/latency measures (brief 14.1, default applied, not confirmed with the site owner). Adapter-specific source mapping (which Epoch AI CSV backs which slug, and so on) deliberately lives in the adapter, not here: this file is the vocabulary, not the plumbing.

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.description: Graduate-level physics, chemistry and biology questions written to be Google-proof. The Diamond subset is the hardest, most expert-validated slice.

benchmarks.name: FrontierMath
benchmarks.description: Unpublished research-level mathematics problems, held private to limit contamination. Tiers 1-3 are hard; Tier 4 is research-frontier.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.description: Real GitHub issues from Python repositories, human-validated as solvable. Scores are meaningless without the scaffold that produced them.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench
benchmarks.description: End-to-end tasks in a real terminal sandbox. Measures an agent plus its harness, not a model on its own.

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI-2
benchmarks.description: Grid puzzles designed so that each task needs a rule inferred from a handful of examples rather than recalled.

benchmarks.name: LiveBench
benchmarks.description: Contamination-limited suite with monthly question refreshes and objective ground truth — no LLM judge. Scores from different question-set months are not comparable.

benchmarks.name: Aider Polyglot
benchmarks.description: Exercism coding exercises across six languages, run through the Aider edit loop. The edit format is part of the result.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam
benchmarks.description: Expert-written questions across a wide range of academic subjects, built to stay hard after the rest of the field saturates.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: A harder, ten-option rebuild of MMLU with the noisiest items removed. Not comparable to plain MMLU.

benchmarks.name: LMArena Text Elo
benchmarks.description: Elo from blind human pairwise preference. A measure of which answer people prefer, not of capability — never mix it into an accuracy comparison.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench
benchmarks.description: Competitive-programming problems collected continuously and filtered by release date, so a model can only be scored on problems published after its cutoff.

benchmarks.name: OSWorld
benchmarks.description: Open-ended computer-use tasks in a real desktop environment, scored by execution rather than by a judge.
